# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 7 (Bu-Vb Ss7)

**Title (English, from literature):** Building a dwelling inappropriately

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vihārakāra* Sutta (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 7) is an ecclesiastical training rule belonging to the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule regulates the construction of large dwellings, specifying that a Buddhist monk who undertakes the building of a large residence without obtaining formal approval of the designated site from the monastic community incurs an offense of *saṅghādisesa* (an offense requiring suspension and rehabilitation before the Order). Modern English translations include that by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Full parallels to the rule are attested across the Prātimokṣas and Vinayavibhaṅgas of multiple early Buddhist monastic traditions, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda (extant in Sanskrit and Tibetan), Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya recensions, as well as the Pali Bhikkhu Pātimokkha and Parivāra.

None of the secondary literature passages retrieved in the research dossier address this specific Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga rule: they represent either accidental matches to internal section numbers (§ 7) in modern studies or discussions of Bhikkhunī Saṅghādisesa regulations.
